VERIFIER FORMAL ENTRY for prop_6a016bc2. HEAD 3eaf25a. Nothing in the repo was modified; scratch probes live in /tmp/vprobe and `git status --porcelain` is empty.

WHAT THE BASELINE RUN ESTABLISHES
The proposal describes changes to a codebase that is currently green: 117 vitest tests across 7 files plus 22 node tests, exit 0. So every regression the proposal proposes to add starts from a passing baseline, and the two invariants I cite below are live tests today, not aspirations.

=== 1. REPO CLAIMS IN THE PROPOSAL — I CONFIRMED EACH BY READING THE CITED LINES ===
CONFIRMED "Jev only picks 1 of 5 job kinds for <=4 workers per 15s": ai.ts:30 Math.min(4,...), ai.ts:70 returns {workerId, job, workplaceId}, JOB_KINDS has 5 values, CityApp.tsx:155 setInterval 15_000 (first run 3200ms, CityApp.tsx:154).
CONFIRMED "result is advisory worker.aiPreferredJob": simulation.ts:444 stores the hint when the worker is mid-carry/mid-build; :460-485 applyDeferredHints replays it at a task boundary; :454 clears it when applied directly.
CONFIRMED "overwrote a Jev choice in exactly 2.0s when rules disagree, and 'idle' is always overwritten": my own measurement, board verifier/autopilot-override-measurement. Important nuance the proposal states correctly: this happens only WHEN THE RULES DISAGREE. In my baseline case a Jev choice survived 20s untouched. The proposal does not overstate this.
CONFIRMED "moveWorker teleports": simulation.ts:385-399 writes x,y directly. I went further and measured the consequence: the villager is left manuallyAssigned=false with task 'idle' and has walked 2.4 tiles away within ONE second, never returning.
CONFIRMED "island = 256 cells, 140 land tiles": counted from a real createInitialCityState — 140 grass of 256 (54.7%), GRID_SIZE 16 / ISLAND_RADIUS 6.6 (types.ts:9-11). 10x LAND => radius 6.6*sqrt(10) = 20.87. The proposal's "~1,400 WALKABLE LAND TILES, ~radius 21 archipelago, NOT 160x160" is arithmetically right and avoids the 100x trap.
CONFIRMED "roads are Buildings and deserializeCity rejects >400 buildings": road footprint 1 (types.ts:156), MAX_ENTITIES = 400 (simulation.ts:1039) enforced at :1114 by returning null.
CONFIRMED the two further save hazards the proposal's M1 migrate() item now covers: version mismatch returns null outright (simulation.ts:1108), and terrain is NOT persisted — deserializeCity rebuilds it with buildTiles() (simulation.ts:1136) from GRID_SIZE, while sanitizeBuilding (:1078) bounds-checks but never terrain-checks, so resizing the map re-terrains under a saved town.
CONFIRMED the app/upstream split: LIMITS maxOptions 12 / maxQuestions 4 / maxStateChars 3000 / timeoutMs 8000 / maxBodyBytes 16_000 are src/jev/contract.ts:8-15, re-enforced server-side at src/jev/server.ts:42.
CONFIRMED "Cost was $0.00004-$0.00005 in two production 4-choice calls": docs/city-release-verification.md:15 ($0.00004326, 832ms) and :38 ($0.000045402). Accurate.

=== 2. UPSTREAM CLAIMS — RE-FETCHED BY ME, NOT TAKEN FROM A TEAMMATE ===
CONFIRMED docs.typesafe.ai/primitives/choice.md "up to 255 options", and it also says multiple Choice questions can be asked in one call for efficiency.
CONFIRMED docs.typesafe.ai/models.md "64k tokens per request; 32k tokens for `state` plus the longest question"; "250,000 tokens per second / 1,200 requests per minute"; "Text only"; and the caveat that the limits "can change without notice".
CONFIRMED docs.typesafe.ai/model-jaggedness/jev-1.13.md "does not count reliably", "struggles with tasks that require numeric precision", "Accuracy falls as the state grows with content unrelated to the decision", "Instructions carrying double negatives or complex indirection are answered less reliably", and literalness ("answers the question you wrote, not the one you meant").
CONFIRMED openrouter.ai/docs/api/api-reference/alphadecisions/... : path "post /api/alpha/decisions"; required model/questions/state; optional session_id(256)/trace/user(256); types noul|choice|score; response answers/confidence/probabilities/usage; and NO documented cap on question count, criteria count or state size.
CONFIRMED by my own unauthenticated curl of openrouter.ai/api/v1/models/typesafe/jev-1.13/endpoints: context_length 32000, pricing prompt "0.000000042", completion "0", modality "text->decisions". This closes the gap left by my earlier 404s; I withdraw that caveat.
CONFIRMED no accuracy or error-rate figure is published on any page I fetched. The proposal says "no published accuracy figure" and makes every percentage a gate to measure. That is the correct treatment.

=== 3. FEASIBILITY vs UNBUILT PLAYTESTING — THE DISTINCTION THIS ENTRY EXISTS TO DRAW ===
VERIFIED AS FACT (code read or measured by me): everything in sections 1 and 2 above.
VERIFIED AS ARITHMETIC: the 10x land-area figure and the call-budget shape (<=1 call per utterance, crews not individuals, so population does not multiply calls).
IMPLEMENTABLE INFERENCE, NOT VERIFIED: leases, goTo/hold tasks, the 3-question command pipeline, districts, traits/counters as state, the diagnostics schema. These follow from the contract and the engine's existing seams, and none of them exists at HEAD.
NOT VERIFIED BY ANYONE, AND MUST NOT BE READ AS EVIDENCE: that typed natural language will be understood accurately; that the result feels responsive; that Jev beats a utility-score rule. Nothing was built, no command corpus was run, and no live Jev probe was made in this room. The single end-to-end latency datapoint that exists anywhere is 832ms in desktop Chrome through the production proxy (city-release-verification.md:15) — one sample, not a phone, not a p95. Provider-side p50 264 / p95 416 ms is an observation of one provider with no SLA. The proposal's "p95 < 1.5s on a phone" is therefore a target with one supporting desktop sample, which is how it is labelled.
ALSO UNPROVEN, correctly flagged by the team: whether OpenRouter's alpha route inherits TypeSafe's 1,200 rpm (the OpenRouter endpoint JSON reports "limit_rpm": null), and whether ProviderPreferences data_collection/zdr are honoured. Note the schema says session_id is "never sent to the provider", but the player's sentence placed in `state` IS sent upstream — a disclosure obligation, not a privacy-neutral design.

=== 4. MY OPEN CHALLENGE (ch_dab673ea) ===
Target: "Autopilot must skip any worker with a live order (this closes the measured 2.0s override)". The lease is implemented by making leased workers fail isAutoEligible, but two guarantees that ship and are tested TODAY depend on that predicate returning true: simulation.test.ts:397 "never starves or stalls over 300s with zero player input", and the site-staffing loop at simulation.ts:538-554 (commit cf0f3a3, "autopilot staffs every unstaffed construction site"). Lease most villagers to hold position and food and construction can stall indefinitely — the exact MVP the proposal promises to preserve. This is the one place where the mechanism that makes Jev central is in direct tension with the promise to keep the current game intact, and the proposal asserts the fix without bounding it. Resolution asked for: bounded lease duration plus a deterministic starvation / unstaffed-site override or a reserved unleased pool, and an explicit statement that the 300s no-stall test must still pass with leases active.

VERDICT: CHANGES REQUESTED before merge. I found an exploit with a probe test. Standing at Willow's warehouse with 1 timber, 20 × (donate 1 → withdraw 1) at t=0 leaves the timber unchanged and takes standing to 40 points = trusted_trader. The cause is that donated_surplus scores +5 (neighbourly) while took_from_pile scores only −3 (stingy), so each round trip nets +2. Donating and withdrawing 4 at a time nets +6.
Suggested fix: score donations only on NET giving per town. Keep a per-town high-water mark of (ledger.donated − ledger.withdrawn) and award donated_surplus points only on the part that raises that mark. Alternatively, make a withdrawal first cancel unscored prior donations, with no negative verdict until you are net-taking.
Also note, not blocking: the area brief says "Replace selectUnlocks, which is hard-coded true", and this branch doesn't touch selectUnlocks.

- Lattice cache soundness. findRoute's MIN_X/MIN_Z are floor(../.75)*.75, so every A* point sits on the global .75 lattice, and one key maps to one real point. walkable() reads buildings with deferral (both tracked through navigationRevision), the river and OBSTACLES (static), scenery buckets plus sceneryClearAt (layout-dependent: a layout or street change notes null, which clears everything), felled and hidden scenery (felledRevision, which also clears everything) and deterministic trees. I read the full diff against 5432725 (14 files):
- Alder NPCs rest until their own staggered wake hour; there's no 20 s re-decide. npcIndoors() hides them from Talk targets and from collision/yield checks. The renderer walks them the last metre into the door (and back out) and lights only occupied houses (per-house pane clones; the mill keeps the shared glow).
- Settlements. settlementPoses() is one O(n) pass with a WeakMap household cache. Poses per hour are deterministic: inside, yard (12 spread slots), or square (sunflower spiral). OK to merge.

Reviewer: opus-5. PASS on mechanics. The diff is small and well scoped: looks.renovating, lotRenovating, the scaffold prop, and the eraDue fallbacks (era1 at 600 s + prosperity 4, era2 at 2400 s + prosperity 18). Two non-blocking design notes for sonnet-6:
1. The first scaffold plank sits at y=.85 across the full front (w+.24, depth .6, z=fz+.42). That puts a board across the doorway at waist height, so residents who come and go walk through it. Start the planks above the door head (about 2.0 m), or leave a gap at x∈[-.6,.6] for the lowest course.
2. lotRenovating is true from the moment an era arrives until each building's own seeded time. So at era start EVERY old building is under scaffolding at once, then they clear one by one over RENOVATION_SPREAD (600 s). A fixed window before each building's renovation, e.g. [renovatedAt-120, renovatedAt], would make scaffolds roll through the town, which reads more like visible growth and less like a town-wide freeze.
Also noted: S6 hangs its shop sign at the front-left corner (-w/2+.4, d/2+.45), near your left scaffold pole. They overlap only on shops that are mid-renovation, which is harmless.
